evidence.evidence_summary: Age-19 freshman breakout (600 yards, Clemson/ACC, Power 4). Career 208 rec / 2,336 yds / 21 TD (PFF). YPRR 2.94 (career, elite efficiency tier); 124.1 passer rating when targeted (81st pct), 10.1% 1D/route run. 55.5% contested catch rate on 20+ aDOT. Inside-outside versatility despite slot label; identical efficiency in slot and out-wide. 75th pct vs man, 64th pct vs zone (Reception Perception). PFF WR11 projection, 2nd-round grade. Named comp screen (non-R1 P4 WR since 2020 with career 75th+ pctile passer rating when targeted + 50th+ pctile TPRR + BOA < 20): George Pickens, Antonio Williams, Elijah Sarratt, Josh Downs, Troy Franklin, Puka Nacua. FP/G floor in years 1-3: 7.4 (Franklin); 3 of 6 above 10+ FP/G. Route profiles estimated pending CFBD fetch.

Transfer path: 470 yards as true freshman at Colorado, injury-limited seasons 2023-24, then 2025 draft cycle at Arizona State. Combine: 26 bench reps (one shy of WR all-time record) — exceptional functional strength for position. Skipped speed/jump testing (hamstring). MTF 0.07 (lowest in class) — profile is separator/route-runner, not YAC threat. Athletic profile is strength-over-speed archetype.

evidence.evidence_summary: Transfer: New Mexico State 2024 (lower competition, weak OL) → Arkansas 2025. Arkansas 2025 OL ranked 110th/133 FBS in sacks allowed; mid-season emergency line adjustments. Production season (62.8 score) was behind one of the worst OLs in FBS. Elite combine profile (4.33 / 39.0 vert / 128 broad, RAS 66) — athleticism is genuine. Red flags: MTF/touch 0.165 (9th-worst Day 2 RB since 2014); YAC+catch 2nd-best season 47.6 yd/game. Scouting consensus: thrives in gap/power with defined lanes; struggles in space; 'often taken down by first tackler' (PFF). OL context is mitigating but doesn't fully explain away the contact quality gap. Gap/power scheme + functional OL is prerequisite for upside.

Transfer: Notre Dame (2024, shared backfield with Jeremiyah Love) → Texas A&M (2025). Breakout at age 20 at Notre Dame despite competing for carries with Love — a top-tier RB1 prospect. Production suppression from shared backfield is mitigating context for volume metrics. Dynasty community ranks him RB2 of class (overall top-5 rookie pick). Red flag: YAC+catch 2nd-best season 39.9 yd/game — among the worst in the top-100 DC RB dataset since 2017 (D.Harris, Sony Michel, Penny, CEH comps). One-hit-wonder risk remains; YAC consistency gap is the primary model concern.

75th+ pctile career YPRR + passer rating when targeted + 50th+ pctile TPRR (non-R1 P4 WR since 2021) — matches Puka Nacua, Tank Dell, Troy Franklin efficiency tier. Nacua comp is strongest: 43-48 rec/yr at BYU (modest volume), 18.3 YPC, 128.0 QB rating when targeted — then 105 catches in NFL year 1 as a 5th-round pick. Efficiency held when target share increased. Sarratt profile: low college volume, elite per-route efficiency — same archetype. Named comp screen (non-R1 P4 WR since 2020 with career 75th+ pctile passer rating when targeted + 50th+ pctile TPRR + BOA < 20): George Pickens, Antonio Williams, Elijah Sarratt, Josh Downs, Troy Franklin, Puka Nacua. FP/G floor in years 1-3: 7.4 (Franklin); 3 of 6 above 10+ FP/G. Late breakout (BOA 21) is model red flag; Aiyuk/Watson are precedents for senior-breakout success, but base rate is poor. MTF 0.13 (mid-tier). Model gap: volume-weighted age-adjusted production (18.2 age-adj, blend → 38) severely underweights efficiency; CFBD raw production score 67.6 is more representative.
evidence.context_source: @ffdataroma research note 2026-04-08 + @ScottBarrettDFB PFF chart + NCAA.com Puka Nacua stats

evidence.evidence_summary: Dual-threat FB/RB/WR from Navy (G5 option offense). 2025: 941 receiving yards + 499 rushing yards, 9 total TDs, 18.3 YPC career average (deep-ball tracker). Elite athleticism: 4.44 40-yard dash + 6.55 3-cone at 6'0" 198lb — best weight-adjusted 3-cone since 2013 per PFF (0.02s faster than CMC at same weight). Named comp group for weight-adjusted 3-cone since 2013: Christian McCaffrey, Le'Veon Bell, David Johnson, Ameer Abdullah; 3 of 10 finished as overall fantasy RB1. One career fumble (elite ball security). Capable blocker. Strong Shrine Bowl week. Concerns: Day 3 projection, Navy triple-option makes college stats difficult to project to NFL, limited arm length (29.25"), limited route tree, not overly elusive in open field. Navy players require DoD waiver to enter draft immediately — presumed granted given model inclusion. G5 BOA penalty (+0.5) applied; effective BOA 22.5 → age multiplier 0.85x (floor). Production score estimated from dual-threat output competition-adjusted.
